The failure depends on the global_random_seed fixture and on where NaNs land after sorting; a seed that places no NaN at the percentile boundary could pass on the buggy revision, so run with several seeds (e.g. --global-random-seed values) to make the transition observable.

No dtype, precision or tolerance is stated in the evidence. The test's comparison is not shown in the diff, so the exact assertion type (for example assert_allclose with default tolerance) is assumed; NaN against a finite value fails under any standard tolerance.
Build requirements for the Cython/meson toolchain and a C compiler are not stated in the evidence; the editable build assumes they are available in the environment.

No platform, architecture, sanitizer, BLAS or threading dependence is evidenced, so the behaviour is expected to be platform-independent; if it is not reproduced on a plain x86_64 Linux build, that would contradict the evidence rather than indicate a missing platform.

NumPy and SciPy versions are only lower-bounded by the README; no era ceiling is documented, so a current release within the bounds is used and any version-sensitive NaN handling in numpy.sort or percentile routines is unverified.
